location: mostly USA and Canada (33-46 N), plus Brazil
cover_crop: non-legume (mostly cereal rye; also oat, oilseed radish, annual rye)
comparison: non-legume cover crop + recommended N fertilizer vs. bare fallow + recommended N fertilizer
metric: percent yield decline of cash crop (mostly corn and sorghum)
quote: Though yields under non-legume cover crop management averaged a 3% decline relative to bare fallow management, the 95% conﬁdence interval overlaps with zero, indicating this decline is not statistically signiﬁcant.
note: Headline result for non-legume cover crops with equal N fertilization; a 3% decline (i.e., -3%). Crops pooled (corn, sorghum, vegetables); not corn-specific. Exact CI only in Fig. 1. Authors note mean is biased by one outlier with a 52% decline. No soybean data in paper.

location: mostly USA and Canada, plus Brazil
cover_crop: legumes (vetches, clovers, alfalfa, field pea, etc.) as green manure
comparison: unfertilized corn after legume cover crop vs. corn with recommended N fertilizer after bare fallow
uncertainty: 95% CI in Fig. 2 (not in text); significant
quote: Relative to conventional systems receiving recommended fertilizer inputs, corn yields in legume-based systems were 12% lower.
note: Corn-specific result (-12%). Confounded with N source: legume treatment received no inorganic N while control received recommended fertilizer. Sorghum yields not significantly different.

location: mostly USA and Canada, plus Brazil
comparison: unfertilized cash crop after legume cover crop vs. recommended N fertilizer after bare fallow
metric: percent yield decline of cash crop (corn, sorghum, vegetables pooled)
uncertainty: 95% CI in Fig. 1 (not in text); significant
quote: Legume-fertilized systems averaged a 10% decline in yield relative to inorganically-fertilized systems with a winter bare fallow.
note: All crops pooled (-10%); legume N replaces fertilizer N. Decline was greater in USDA hardiness zone 4.

location: mostly USA and Canada, plus Brazil
comparison: unfertilized cash crop after legume cover crop vs. fertilized bare fallow at all control fertilizer levels (low, recommended, high)
metric: percent yield decline of cash crop
quote: As a result, the overall effect size under all fertilizations tested was a 7% decline in yield in legume relative to conventional systems.
note: Includes low-fertilizer controls, against which legume systems averaged a 5% yield improvement.

location: mostly USA and Canada, plus Brazil
comparison: unfertilized cash crop after legume cover crop vs. recommended N fertilizer after bare fallow
metric: percent yield decline of cash crop
quote: There was a measurable difference in yield when legume biomass was reduced, with a moderate legume input of 80–110 kg N ha1 averaging a 15% yield decline, while legume inputs <80 kg N ha1 averaged a 19% yield decline relative to conventional systems.
note: Moderator: legume N input. With 110-180 kg N ha-1 there was no yield difference, and with >180 kg N ha-1 yields averaged 5% higher. The minus sign in 'ha-1' was lost in text extraction.

location: mostly USA and Canada, plus Brazil
comparison: unfertilized cash crop after legume cover crop vs. recommended N fertilizer after bare fallow
metric: percent yield decline of cash crop
quote: There was a measurable difference in yield when legume biomass was reduced, with a moderate legume input of 80–110 kg N ha1 averaging a 15% yield decline, while legume inputs <80 kg N ha1 averaged a 19% yield decline relative to conventional systems.
note: Moderator: low legume N input. The minus sign in 'ha-1' was lost in text extraction.
